type_constraints.description: class field must be CamelCase (capital first letter, alphanumeric only)
vectorIndexType must be one of: hnsw, flat, dynamic
properties[].dataType must be array of valid types or class references
type_constraints.assertion: properties[].dataType is array of strings; first-capital values are class references

type_constraints.description: properties[].tokenization must be valid enum value
id must be valid UUID format (v4 or v7)
vector must be array of floats
id must be URL-safe (lowercase, numbers, underscore, minus only)
namespace_id must be lowercase letters, digits, hyphens only

state_constraints.description: schema is RAFT-replicated across the cluster
state_constraints.assertion: schema changes are replicated via RAFT consensus

state_constraints.description: permanently deletes all data objects and references (cascade delete)
state_constraints.assertion: deleting collection cascades to all objects and references
PUT collection does not add properties; use separate endpoint

state_constraints.description: after cursor is mutually exclusive with offset and sort
state_constraints.assertion: after cannot be used with offset or sort parameters

state_constraints.description: idempotent by UUID -- existing UUIDs overwritten (PUT semantics per item)
state_constraints.assertion: batch create is idempotent; existing UUIDs are replaced
usage limit exceeded rejects entire batch, no partial success

state_constraints.description: null fields are removed (RFC 7396 JSON merge patch)
state_constraints.assertion: null values in PATCH remove fields

state_constraints.description: include and exclude are mutually exclusive
state_constraints.assertion: include and exclude cannot both be specified

state_constraints.description: target cluster must have same node count and node names as source
state_constraints.assertion: restore requires matching node count and names

state_constraints.description: collections must not already exist on target
state_constraints.assertion: restore fails if collections already exist
deleting tenant cascades to all tenant data

state_constraints.description: must start and end with letter or digit
state_constraints.assertion: namespace_id must start and end with alphanumeric character

assertions.description: liveness check returns 200 when application is alive
readiness check returns 200 when ready, 503 when not ready
POST fails with error if id already exists (use PUT to replace or PATCH to update)
assertions.expected_behavior: fails with error if id already exists

assertions.description: PUT creates object if id does not exist (upsert semantics)

assertions.expected_behavior: usage limit exceeds rejects entire batch

assertions.description: 202 task submitted (async reindex); 409 conflicting reindex running
assertions.expected_behavior: 202 if reindex submitted; 409 if conflicting reindex running

behavioral_contracts.description: Created collection is immediately queryable via GraphQL
behavioral_contracts.scenario: POST /schema creates collection -> GraphQL Get queries succeed
behavioral_contracts.expected_behavior: Collection is visible in schema and can be queried immediately after creation

behavioral_contracts.description: Deleted collection is not queryable and returns 404
behavioral_contracts.scenario: DELETE /schema/{className} -> GraphQL Get /schema GET return 404 or empty
behavioral_contracts.expected_behavior: Collection is removed from schema; queries return 404
Object is readable after creation, updates are visible, deletion makes it inaccessible

behavioral_contracts.description: Batch operations maintain atomicity at batch level
behavioral_contracts.scenario: POST /batch/objects with usage limit exceeded -> 429 rejects entire batch
behavioral_contracts.expected_behavior: No partial success on usage limit exceeded; entire batch fails

behavioral_contracts.description: Backup and restore preserve collection data and schema
behavioral_contracts.expected_behavior: Restored collections have same schema and data as backup

behavioral_contracts.scenario: POST /schema/{className}/tenants (tenant=A) -> POST /objects (tenant=A) -> GET /objects (tenant=B) -> objects not visible
behavioral_contracts.expected_behavior: Data is isolated per tenant; cross-tenant queries return empty

state_invariants.description: Creating collection increases collection count by 1
state_invariants.assertion: POST /schema -> GET /schema returns collections[] with new collection

state_invariants.description: Creating N objects increases object count by N
state_invariants.assertion: POST N objects -> GET /objects returns totalResults = previous + N

state_invariants.description: Deleting collection removes all objects and returns 404
state_invariants.assertion: DELETE /schema/{className} -> GET /objects?class=className returns empty; GET /schema/{className} returns 404
POST /objects/{className}/{id}/references/{propertyName} -> GET shows reference; DELETE target -> reference still exists (Weaviate uses soft references)
